terms.def: Abbreviated New Drug Application: the application for a generic drug, which relies on the reference listed drug.
A copy of the label with notes linking each statement to its source (study, CCDS section, agency request).
A warning in a box at the start of the FPI for serious risks; summarised in Highlights in no more than 20 lines.
The outer package label. Carries more information than the container label.
Leaving a protected indication out of generic labeling under a section viii statement.
Changes Being Effected supplement: some labeling changes, such as strengthening a warning, can be implemented when the supplement is submitted.
Company Core Data Sheet: the company's global reference for a product's safety and use, against which local labels are compared (Phase 2).
Company Core Safety Information: the safety part of the CCDS.
The label on the immediate container, such as a bottle or vial.
A pointer to another section, written as "[see Warnings and Precautions (5.3)]".
The public website that publishes SPL labeling for marketed products.
The official non-proprietary name of the drug, such as lumiravostat.
Full Prescribing Information: the 17 numbered sections after Highlights and the table of contents.
The half-page summary at the top of a PLR prescribing information.
Instructions for Use: step-by-step patient labeling for products with complex use.
All written, printed or graphic matter on or accompanying a drug.
A coding system; in SPL, LOINC codes identify each labeling section.
FDA-approved patient labeling required under 21 CFR 208 for certain products with serious risks.
A decimal without a leading zero (".5 mg"). Write "0.5 mg".
National Drug Code: a 10-digit identifier for labeler, product and package (4-4-2, 5-3-2 or 5-4-1).
The labeling format in 21 CFR 201.80, used before PLR, with unnumbered sections.
Prescribing information: the label written for health professionals.
Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Rule (in effect 30 June 2015): replaced letter categories with 8.1, 8.2 and 8.3.
Physician Labeling Rule (2006): the Highlights plus 17-section format in 21 CFR 201.57.
Patient Medication Information: a proposed one-page patient sheet (2023 proposal, not final).
Patient Package Insert: patient labeling required for some classes and voluntary for others.
The printer's artwork, checked word by word against approved text before printing.
A Highlights list of recent substantive changes to the Boxed Warning or sections 1, 2, 4 or 5.
The approved drug a generic is compared with and whose labeling it follows.
The opening of 8.1 and 8.2 under PLLR, integrating data into a statement of risk.
A statement in an ANDA that it does not seek approval for a patented method of use.
Structured Product Labeling: the HL7 XML format FDA uses to receive labeling.
A zero after a decimal point ("5.0 mg"), which can cause tenfold errors.
In this app, a recorded reason for accepting a warning without changing the text. Errors cannot be waived.
The FD&C Act power for FDA to require safety labeling changes; the holder has 30 days to respond.
